newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian parliament lower house clears fund bill.
newsitem.headline: Romanian parliament lower house clears fund bill.

text.p: The Romanian parliament's lower chamber on Wednesday passed a bill converting five regional private ownership funds (FPPs) into U.S.-style mutual funds as part of a mass privatisation programme.
The bill to turn the five FPPs into "financial investment companies" starting November 1 cleared the upper Senate last month and must secure presidential approval.
"With their transformation pending, promulgation by the president is to be expected very soon," a parliamentary spokesman said.

The FPPs were formed in 1991 under a privatisation law to manage 30 percent of around 6,500 state companies on behalf of 15.5 million Romanians who got free vouchers representing that stake. The majority 70 percent stockholder of those companies is the centrally-run State Ownership Fund.
Turning the FPPs into investment companies is part of a mass selloff started last October allowing Romanians to swap vouchers for up to 60 percent of around 4,000 enterprises.
Romanians' other option for their privatisation paper was placing it with one of the five FPPs in return for shares of these funds.
Shares of the FPPs turned investment companies can be traded on Romania's capital market, according to the bill.
Romania's stock exchange has been in operation for almost a year and an over-the-counter (OTC) market is being tested before going into trading later this month.
Stock traders welcomed the new investment companies, saying they could partially fill the gap of big institutional investors in Romania's budding capital market.
"They will certainly bring to the market the capital liquidity it badly needs," one trader said.
